chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said:
I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'For what reason has it become that the pilgrim is not recorded with sin for four months?'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, permitted the Polytheists the Sanctuary for four months, when He said: So go about in the land for four months. Then He gifted to those from the Believers who perform Hajj of the House, the sins [as a gift] for four months.'
ai.seo_question: Why are sins forgiven for four months after performing Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual mechanics of Hajj by drawing a parallel between the temporal grace granted to the Polytheists and the spiritual expiation bestowed upon Believers. Just as Surah At-Tawbah granted the Mushrikeen four months of safe passage (*tawqif*) to observe the rites, Allah has gifted the faithful with a four-month period of sin forgiveness (*kaffarah*) through the performance of Hajj. This comparison highlights the transition from physical safety to spiritual purification, emphasizing the unique merit of the pilgrimage in erasing past transgressions.
